The reported dependency cycle is between **files**, so redirecting `Jason.Encode` to that new module would still leave its compile-time dependency on `lib/codegen.ex`.

The two saved reports—[all cycles](observed/all-cycles.txt) and [compile-connected cycles](observed/compile-connected.txt)—both report one three-file cyclic group containing one compile edge. They do **not** establish that all three edges are compile-time dependencies. The saved traces identify the crossing: [lib/encode.ex](lib/encode.ex:284) calls `Codegen.jump_table` three times while defining escape functions; [lib/codegen.ex](lib/codegen.ex:106) calls `Encode.key` for generated map encoding at runtime; and [lib/encoder.ex](lib/encoder.ex:77) links the deriving path back to Codegen. The reports are a baseline, not a measured result of either proposal.

This is a bounded file-boundary change aimed at the compile-connected cycle. A runtime cycle may remain, and I would report it separately rather than claim that this move removes every cycle.
